TITLE:
Social Proof:
When the Crowd
Becomes the Evidence
LEAD: When you're not sure what's true or what to do, other people's behavior carries real information — if a hundred people just walked out of a building, that's evidence something's wrong, even before you smell smoke. That's rational, not just herd instinct. But it creates a threshold effect: your own uncertainty barely moves while only a few others have acted, then collapses fast once enough have — which is why adoption of anything uncertain (a new tool, a rumor, an evacuation) tends to look flat, then suddenly tip, rather than climb steadily.
